_meta.indication: XERAVA is a tetracycline class antibacterial indicated for the treatment of complicated intra-abdominal infections in patients 18 years of age and older; not indicated for cUTI.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, comparative, noninferiority
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, comparative noninferiority trial of eravacycline IV 1.0 mg/kg q12h vs ertapenem IV 1 g q24h, with a pre-specified NI margin of 10%.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection (cIAI), 18-75 years, male and female.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical response (clinical cure) at Test-of-Cure (Day 25-31) in the micro-ITT population.
pivotal_trials.n: Eravacycline arm 270, ertapenem arm 271 randomized; micro-ITT N=220 vs 226.
pivotal_trials.result: Non-inferiority demonstrated: clinical cure 191 (86.8%) eravacycline vs 198 (87.6%) ertapenem, difference -0.8% (95% CI -7.1, 5.5), lower limit exceeding the -10% NI margin.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, comparative, noninferiority
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, comparative noninferiority trial of eravacycline IV 1.0 mg/kg q12h vs meropenem IV 1.0 g q8h, with a pre-specified NI margin of 12.5%.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with complicated intra-abdominal infection (cIAI), 18-75 years, male and female.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical response (clinical cure) at Test-of-Cure (Day 25-31) in the micro-ITT population.
pivotal_trials.n: Eravacycline arm 250, meropenem arm 250 randomized; micro-ITT N=195 vs 205.
pivotal_trials.result: Non-inferiority demonstrated: clinical cure 177 (90.8%) eravacycline vs 187 (91.2%) meropenem, difference -0.5% (95% CI -6.3, 5.3), lower limit exceeding the -12.5% NI margin.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=3%) were infusion site reactions (7.7% vs 1.9% comparator), nausea (6.5% vs 0.6%), and vomiting (3.7% vs 2.5%). Major risks include life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions, tooth discoloration/enamel hypoplasia, inhibition of bone growth, and C. difficile-associated diarrhea.
target_moa: Eravacycline is a synthetic tetracycline-class (fluorocyclic) antibacterial that binds the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis; activity is bacteriostatic.

rems.type: No safety signals require a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy; routine postmarketing surveillance suffices.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was not convened for this NDA.

summary.text: XERAVA (eravacycline), a Type 1 NME 505(b)(1) NDA, received QIDP and Fast Track designations for cIAI/cUTI and was granted Priority review, receiving traditional approval based on two Phase 3 noninferiority trials in cIAI; no advisory committee was convened and no accelerated approval was used.

citations.quote: July 9, 2013: Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) was granted for IV eravacycline for the indications of cIAI and cUTI.
March 27, 2014: Fast track designation was granted for IV eravacycline for the indications of cIAI and cUTI.
This new drug application provided data from two adequate and well-controlled, randomized clinical trials to conclude noninferiority of XERAVA relative to comparators in the treatment of cIAI.

requirement.text: 3472-1: Conduct a study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability of a single dose of intravenous XERAVA in pediatric patients from 8 years to less than 18 years of age with suspected or confirmed bacterial infection.

requirement.text: 3472-2: Conduct a randomized, multicenter, active-controlled trial to evaluate the safety and tolerability of intravenous XERAVA in pediatric patients from 8 years to less than 18 years of age with complicated intra-abdominal infections.
